title: Del LaGrace Volcano: Sensual / Mutual
blurb: Unseen 70s and 80s work from a leather dyke bar, a rent-striking artist hotel and a women's land commune. Tender rather than nostalgic, and closing next weekend.

title: Rio Forever: 50 Years of the Rio
blurb: The community-run Dalston landmark celebrates its half-century with archival gems, 35mm prints and guest intros through October. Support your local picture palace.

title: All Kaiju Attack: All Stars!
blurb: Two months of monster mayhem: Godzilla, Ghidorah and friends stomping through a properly curated kaiju season. City-crushing on a big screen, as intended.

title: A Road Less Travelled: Harry Dean Stanton
blurb: Fifty years of the greatest face in American cinema: Paris, Texas, Repo Man and the character-actor deep cuts. Every screening a masterclass in doing less.

title: Claude Chabrol: Elements of Crime
blurb: Two months of poisonous bourgeois thrillers from the Nouvelle Vague's Hitchcockian, with a companion strand at the ICA (11, 25 Sep). Le Boucher with a glass of something red is the correct autumn ritual.

title: Monika Sosnowska: Weight of Matter
blurb: Modernist steel and concrete twisted into hanging tangles across both SLG buildings, plus her paper maquettes shown in London for the first time. Post-communist architecture with the stuffing knocked out.

title: Liz Larner: A hard line to bend
blurb: The LA sculptor's first major UK institutional show: ceramic asteroids named after mythic women, slabs of glaze and a new bronze Lilith. Matter behaving strangely, as promised.

title: Martine Syms: Knot Eye
blurb: Two new films, a New Orleans docu-fantasy and a drunk late-night apartment story, plus a concept store that is also an artwork. Peak Syms, in Soho.

title: Evelyn Taocheng Wang: Being Poetic Ruins Life
blurb: Agnes Martin grids smuggled into Chinese calligraphy, seals and pop culture figures, in her first UK institutional show. That title alone earns the trip to New Cross.

title: Autumn Knight: I Can't Complain
blurb: A balloon canopy and a sound piece built from people's everyday irritations, in the New York performer's first major UK show. Finally, an exhibition about moaning, in London.

title: Mohammad Alfaraj: The heart is a bird's nest, the brain is a spider web
blurb: Former resident returns to Delfina's townhouse to imagine home as an ecosystem where insects and plants count as family. Domestic setting, used properly for once.

title: Imogen Stidworthy: Skydde
blurb: Three years filming a Swedish therapeutic group practice, broken into zones of structure, sound, video and bronze, with six artists' audio guides leading you through. Listening as a full body sport.

title: Paloma Contreras Lomas: Disco Inferno
blurb: Room-sized murals, a plush sculpture and a 15 minute film retelling Mexico's cartel war years as darkly comic hell. Folklore and pop culture doing grim overtime in Vauxhall.

title: Yuko Mohri: In Concert
blurb: Kinetic sculpture driven by magnetism, humidity and gravity, using objects borrowed from the Barbican itself. A self-playing orchestra of household junk that never performs the same set twice.

title: Wakaliga Uganda: Kibuuka Omumbaale
blurb: Wakaliwood, Kampala's ultra low budget action film factory, premieres a new commission about a Baganda warrior god. Supa-action in Bow, which is not a sentence you get often.

title: Wakaliga Uganda: new commission
blurb: The Wakaliwood studio premieres a newly commissioned film on the warrior Kibuuka Omumbaale. Ugandan no-budget action cinema meets the London commission circuit, the autumn's most improbable opening.

title: 70th BFI London Film Festival
blurb: The big one turns 70. The Treasures strand is where rep heads should aim: restorations and archive premieres galore.

title: Cecilia Vicuña: Living Threads
blurb: Six decades of quipus, precarios and her 1970s London paintings, plus the archive of Artists for Democracy, which she co-founded a few miles from the gallery. A homecoming of sorts.

title: Katherine Hubbard: The Great Room
blurb: Five years of caring for her mother through a degenerative brain disease, rendered as big black and white photographs, sightline-blocking walls and contact prints made together on the paper. Quietly devastating.

title: Jeff Preiss: Orchard Documents
blurb: The cinematographer and diarist filmmaker on Orchard, the much mythologised Lower East Side artist-run gallery. Downtown New York institutional memory in a Cambridge Heath project space.

title: Justin Caguiat: Change Ringing
blurb: Hazy, densely worked painting from the Filipino-American artist, named after the mathematical English art of bell ringing. Kensington Gardens in winter is the right light for it.

title: Rebecca Warren: There Will Be Another You
blurb: Warren's lumpen, knowing sculpture spread across both Bethnal Green spaces, Herald Street and Three Colts Lane. Make a crawl of it with Cell and Chisenhale.

title: Sturtevant: Eat the Outside to Light Up the Inside
blurb: The first UK institutional show since her death: a room of Warhols that aren't Warhols, rare Krazy Kat drawings and a cutout moon to sit on. Repetition as the most radical gesture in the room.

title: Divine Noise All-Dayer #2
blurb: Seven acts of scuzz, skronk and squall from Snorkel, Meat Strap, Drum Tower, Brabble and friends in the Manor House DIY space.

title: the87press present Mushaira
blurb: A poetry gathering in the Urdu mushaira tradition, with CAConrad and Roger Robinson on the bill and a Chef Yogi kitchen keeping everyone fed. Tonight, so move fast.

title: If Music presents Left Turn
blurb: Sunday afternoon jungle and drum and bass from the If Music crew with Suburban Architecture on decks and LyricL on the mic. Home by ten, ears ringing.

title: Library of the Occult: Ye Gods (Antoni Maiovvi)
blurb: Giallo-synth auteur Antoni Maiovvi's Ye Gods project headlines a Library of the Occult label night under the Three Crowns, kosmische for the candle-lit set.

title: The Hart of London (1970) on 16mm
blurb: Jack Chambers' haunted Canadian found footage landmark, on 16mm where it belongs.

title: The Shining [UK Version] on 35mm
blurb: Kubrick's tighter European cut, the one missing 25 minutes, on 35mm right through Horroctober.

title: Throbbing Gristle: TG50
blurb: Fifty years after Prostitution scandalised the ICA, a free day of TG on the spatial sound system, plus screenings of Heathen Earth and Kezar Pavilion and Chris Carter and Cosey Fanni Tutti in conversation (ticketed separately).

title: deep:listening with Rrose, Akeim Toussaint Buck, Xin
blurb: A sober dancefloor experiment: a group listen to Éliane Radigue's Occam I, movement by Akeim Toussaint Buck scored by Xin, then Rrose's hypnotic, drone-minded techno. Tea bar, no chat during the pieces.

title: Almost Perfect: The Films of Billy Wilder
blurb: Thirty plus films across ten weeks, from Sunset Boulevard to The Apartment, plus Lubitsch, Hawks and People on Sunday for context. Panel with Jonathan Coe on 4 Nov.

title: Death Masks: The Final Portrait with Nick Reynolds
blurb: Sculptor Nick Reynolds, son of Great Train Robber Bruce, on casting the faces of the dead across cultures and centuries. Exactly the right room on Mare Street for it.

title: Feedback Moves: Niloofar Asghary / Conal Blake + Rory Salter / Paul Abbott + Phil Julian / Zheng Hao
blurb: Three first-time or near-first-time duos from Conal Blake's label: no-input mixer feedback, unstable modular systems and XT's drummer meeting a London sound artist. Free for members, which is the right price for a Monday of glorious unknowns.

title: Book Launch + Screening + Q&A: Positions by K8 Hardy
blurb: MACK launches K8 Hardy's Position Series photobook with a screening of Outfitumentary, a decade of her getting dressed on camera. Nina Manandhar does the Q&A.

title: Evan Parker / Steve Swell / Mark Tokar / Klaus Kugel
blurb: Parker's tenor against Steve Swell's trombone over a Ukrainian/German rhythm section that has been grinding together for years. Free jazz as conversation, not spectacle.

title: Faust: 100th Anniversary with Live Score
blurb: Murnau's Faust turns 100, with a live score by mutterichbindoom for SECT Silent Club.

title: Bar Trash 250: Destroy All Monsters
blurb: Bar Trash hits its 250th screening with Honda's kaiju free for all. Themed drinks, intermissions, prizes and cake.

title: I Am Furious Black: The Films of William Greaves
blurb: A full survey of the Black Journal pioneer, built around both Symbiopsychotaxiplasm films, with Souls of Sin and Miracle in Harlem on 35mm on 3 Nov.

title: Kennington Bioscope: The Arrival from the Darkness (1921)
blurb: A Czech silent horror rarity, the Bioscope's Halloween offering in the old Lambeth workhouse.

title: Nebbia / Downes / Lisle: Exhaust
blurb: Camila Nebbia's sax, Kit Downes' piano and Andrew Lisle's knotty drumming, launching their Intakt record with fully spontaneous trio playing.

title: Video Bazaar presents: Possession (North American Cut)
blurb: The butchered 81 minute US theatrical cut of Zulawski's masterpiece, closing the Garden's retrospective. A curio for completists.

title: Abstract Concrete + Borough Council + NPA + PopStar
blurb: Charles Hayward (This Heat) and his band of agitated art-rock lifers at IKLECTIK's new Peckham Levels home. Drums as weather system.

title: Haxan with Live Score
blurb: Benjamin Christensen's 1922 witchcraft essay film, part documentary, part fever dream, with a live score from Hugo Max.

title: The Lower Depths: The Cinema of Shohei Imamura
blurb: The first major UK Imamura retrospective in 25 years: Pigs and Battleships, The Insect Woman, Vengeance is Mine, The Ballad of Narayama, plus 16mm and 35mm rarities.

title: Club Romantico x MOT: Dengue Dengue Dengue, Florentino & Pochola
blurb: Lima's masked duo play their psychedelic cumbia-meets-bass live, with Florentino's reggaeton-tinged club edits to follow. Latin club music at its most mutant.

title: PULSE: School of the Damned
blurb: The peer-led alt art school takes the Upper Gallery for performance, sound and moving image on Stuart Hall's idea of conjuncture. Opening night features an artist self-tattooing, with audience members on the foot pedal.

title: Classic Horror Marathon
blurb: The Thing, The Exorcist, The Shining, Elm Street and Texas Chain Saw back to back on 35mm and DCP, finishing around 8.38am. Sold out at time of writing; watch for returns.

title: Hannah Peel & Beibei Wang + Underland performed by Shards
blurb: Peel's analogue synths meet Beibei Wang's percussion, then the vocal collective Shards premiere Underland. Part of the Always, Already There weekend.

title: IKLECTIKA 5th Edition
blurb: IKLECTIK's annual noon-till-late gathering of experimental sound, now in Peckham. Expect a long day of electronics, improv and things that are hard to categorise.

title: Loefah
blurb: The DMZ co-founder and Swamp 81 boss, the man who kept dubstep's sub-bass sparse and menacing, with GEM (UK) in support. Old south London lore in a former MOT garage.

title: Movementt: Emma-Jean Thackray & Lagoon Lurve
blurb: The jazz trumpeter and bandleader swaps horn for decks, digging through spiritual jazz, broken beat and house in a Rye Lane arch.

title: Mystery Horror Movie Marathon
blurb: Five horror films, titles withheld until the lights go down, 500 minutes through the night. Strictly 18+, no admission after midnight.

title: Pure Poison
blurb: Drop-in afternoon on poisons in medicine, fashion and folklore, with archive reproductions, sniffable scents and mandrake lore. Free and suitably pre-Halloween.

title: Carl Stone + Excel DJ + Silvia Kastel (DJ)
blurb: The LA sampling pioneer chops pop, field recordings and restaurant menus into giddy, looping laptop collage. Silvia Kastel on the decks keeps things properly strange.

title: Cine-Real Halloween: Dead of Night + The Evil Dead on 16mm
blurb: Cine-Real's projectors come out for Ealing's portmanteau classic and Raimi's cabin, both on 16mm. Listed as sold out; check for returns.

title: Concrete Atlantis Present: The Megalithic Imperative
blurb: Launch of a 3rd Stone anthology of earth mysteries writing, with editor Neil Mortimer in conversation, then Urthona (Mortimer plus Mark Pilkington) playing standing stone drone. Hosted by Stonecirclesampler and Travis Elborough.

title: In the Round: Shane Parish, Autechre Guitar
blurb: Ahleuchatistas guitarist translating Autechre's fractured machine logic onto six acoustic strings, played in the round. A stunt that turns out to be genuinely beautiful.

title: Nosferatu with Live Score
blurb: Murnau's original rat king, scored live by Hugo Max across three Halloween week screenings including the night itself.

title: SPACE: Lisa Ullén / Elsa Bergman / Anna Lund
blurb: Swedish piano trio that treats the format as architecture: Lisa Ullén's dense clusters, Elsa Bergman's bowed bass and Anna Lund's patient, textural drums.

title: In the Round: Duet Emmo + Nik Colk Void
blurb: Daniel Miller, Graham Lewis and B.C. Gilbert give their 1983 Mute one-off its world premiere live outing, 45 years late, on the ICA's 360 degree rig. Nik Colk Void supports with voice, guitar and Eurorack.

title: Bill Walton: A Form of Honesty
blurb: Ten small sculptures in lead, copper, glass and textile by a self-taught Philadelphia commercial printer who refused to date his work. Materials pretending to be other materials, beautifully.

title: Bone Folder + Matthew Bourne
blurb: Matthew Bourne, the pianist who swings between Monk, Moog and broken upright pianos, in the basement at SJQ. Intimate and liable to go anywhere.

title: Discrepant vs Keroxen London Festival 2026
blurb: Three nights of Discrepant's wonky collage universe crossed with Tenerife's Keroxen: People Like Us, DJ Sniff, Memotone, Ale Hop, Black Affrontit and Spencer Clark's Light Abductions. Every ticket comes with a free record.

title: Neil Bartlett & Richard Scott on Jarman's Kicking the Pricks
blurb: Two queer writers on Derek Jarman's 1987 diary-manifesto of Super 8, Dungeness and fury. Bartlett knew the era firsthand.

title: Exploding Cinema: 30th October
blurb: London's open access underground film collective: anyone's shorts, live music, heckling, Q&As. The scrappy heart of DIY cinema.

title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
blurb: The PCC's long-running audience participation Rocky, with Halloween weekend dates and encores into late November and December. All listed dates showing sold out, so pounce on returns.

title: Spellbound at The Society of Antiquaries
blurb: Witch bottles, bellarmine spirit houses and a 17th century physician's notebook come out at Burlington House, plus amulet making and a cocktail. Geoffrey Munn presents a Tudor charmstone.

title: Vampire Ball: Live Violin, Cocktails + The Hunger
blurb: Bowie, Deneuve and Tony Scott's smoke machine, preceded by live violin and cocktails. Fruits on Film's first event.

title: mi-el presents Pulling Threads w/ Kelman Duran, ojoo, Lord Tusk
blurb: Kelman Duran's slowed, smeared dembow and reggaeton ghosts alongside Lord Tusk's dubbed-out oddities. Club music that feels like a fever dream.

title: 5 Gate Temple Halloween: Nkisi / Junior Loves / D. Phylleia / Landlock (live)
blurb: Nkisi's polyrhythmic hard-drum ritualism heads a Samhain edition billed as the last 5 Gate Temple for a while. Masks encouraged.

title: Buss with AliA b2b Alex Nut, Sharnie, Cam Joon
blurb: Three hours of Alex Nut (Swamp81, NTS) going back to back with AliA, two diggers who can move from UK funky to Brazilian edits without a seam.

title: Circuit des Yeux feat. Alan Sparhawk presents Nosferatu (1922)
blurb: Haley Fohr's operatic baritone and Low's Alan Sparhawk improvise a new score for Murnau's vampire. Halloween done with taste.

title: Echogenic Halloween
blurb: Afternoon-to-evening Halloween session at the tiny Morning Lane bar with Beaven, Myff Busta, Nio-B, PANACEA and Toad.xp b2b Somewhat Simian. Cheap, sweaty, done by nine.

title: Halloween Marathon
blurb: All six Michael Myers outings from the 1978 original to the Curse Producer's Cut, 617 minutes on Halloween night itself. Pace yourself around Season of the Witch.

title: First Scares with Matthew Sweet
blurb: Matthew Sweet hosts an afternoon of early screen horror. Two shows.

title: Fred Frith: Two-Night Residency
blurb: Henry Cow reunion of sorts with Tim Hodgkinson and Liz Allbee on night one, then Frith solo and in duo with Anne Bourne. Prepared guitar from the man who more or less wrote the manual.

title: Ken Russell's The Devils: The Director's Cut
blurb: Russell's still scandalous Loudun possession epic, restored to the director's cut and shown on 35mm for one week in early November.

title: Eyes Wide Shut on 35mm
blurb: Kubrick's last and most Christmassy film on 35mm, scattered through November and December. The password is Fidelio.

title: Globe Unity Orchestra: Three-Day Residency
blurb: Schlippenbach's free jazz big band turns 60 with fifteen players squeezed into OTO, including Evan Parker, Axel Dörner, Aki Takase and Paul Lytton. History, loudly.

title: Neo-Noirvember
blurb: A month of paranoia, revenge and bad decisions: Heat, Thief and Night Moves on 35mm alongside Cure, Ms. 45, Mikey and Nicky and In a Lonely Place.

title: The Last of England + Intro and Book Launch
blurb: Derek Jarman's Super 8 apocalypse, introduced by Gareth Evans with a book launch.

title: Upset The Rhythm: A People's History of Music
blurb: Eric Isaacson's slideshow lecture on music scenes that kept going under dictatorships, from Ethiopia and Cambodia to North Korea, with archival film and sound.

title: The Conch
blurb: Live art work in progress from Georgina Hill, Alia Hamaoui and Beatrice Vorster on the home as a site of labour and performance, then a group crit. Starts sharp.

title: Vinyl Requiem 33.3: Philip Jeck & Lol Sargent
blurb: 33.3 years after 180 Dansettes filled this chapel, the film of Jeck and Sargent's 1993 Vinyl Requiem is screened at full scale, with a Q&A and Touch's new double-vinyl edition. Profits go to the Philip Jeck Foundation.

title: Accidental Meetings & Meakusma present: Flora Yin Wong & Jerzy Maczynski + Ibrahim Alfa Jnr + opo + Elijah Minnelli
blurb: The Belgian Meakusma festival brings its tilted dub-and-drone sensibility to Dalston, with Flora Yin Wong's ritual ambience paired with Jerzy Maczynski and a run of left-field live sets.

title: Firestations + Dominie Hooper
blurb: London band Firestations share the Stoke Newington basement with cellist and composer Dominie Hooper, whose looped, eerie bow work is the reason to go early.

title: Katie Shannon: BACK/PRUNE/VIRGIN/RUIN
blurb: Glasgow artist who treats the event itself as the medium, drawing on peripheral music histories and feminist ideas of time. Go to the opening on 5 November; that is probably the work.

title: Kantarion Sound: upsammy, Hermeneia, Vanja Rakić, Olgica, ex.sses
blurb: Balkan sound system's London debut, with upsammy's squelchy, playful IDM-leaning sets and a crew of Belgrade selectors on dubby, trippy electronics.

title: Dead Souls + Alex Cox Q&A
blurb: Alex Cox's Gogol by way of spaghetti western, with Cox himself on stage afterwards. Expect tangents.

title: Evan Parker Matinee Residency: Feedbaxophone with Henry Dagg
blurb: Sunday afternoon Parker paired with Henry Dagg, the sound sculptor behind the Sharpsichord, on something billed as the Feedbaxophone. Exactly as odd as it sounds.

title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed with Live Score
blurb: Lotte Reiniger's 1926 silhouette animation, the oldest surviving animated feature, with Hugo Max on live score. Two Wednesday evenings only.

title: The Odyssey in 70mm
blurb: Nolan's Homeric blockbuster in 70mm on the Leicester Square screen, which is exactly how he would want you to see it. Nine dates through November.

title: Lisa Robertson & Iain Sinclair: Riverwork
blurb: The Canadian poet of weather and cities meets London's chief psychogeographer. Expect digressions about water.

title: Movie Maverick: 100 Years of Roger Corman
blurb: Centenary season for the king of the B picture: Poe cycle, Little Shop of Horrors, The Trip. Julie, Catherine and Mary Corman introduce screenings across the 12 to 14 Nov weekend.

title: R&R by SHERELLE
blurb: SHERELLE's new Thursday series: expect footwork, jungle and 160bpm everything from the fastest hands in London. Early tickets were £10.

title: Serious Pleasures: The Life of Stephen Tennant, book launch
blurb: Philip Hoare relaunches his biography of the brightest of the Bright Young Things, the man who stayed in bed. Doubles as the opening of a show of Tennant's own art and ephemera.

title: HomoElectric
blurb: Manchester's long-running queer mixed party brings its disco-to-acid, anyone-welcome ethos down Surrey Canal Road.

title: Kennington Bioscope Silent Laughter Weekend 2026
blurb: Two days of silent comedy with live accompaniment, from Max Linder UK premieres to a 28mm projector show, ending with Keaton's The General at 100.

title: The Lord Mayor's Show
venue: Mansion House to Royal Courts of Justice
blurb: An 800 year old procession in which a new Lord Mayor rides a golden coach to swear loyalty to the Crown. Livery companies, giants and pikemen included, free from the kerb.

title: The Phantom of the Opera + Live Score
blurb: Lon Chaney's 1925 unmasking with a new score played live by Andrew Wasylyk and Tommy Perman. Sold out; members' waiting list.

title: Unhomed/Unravelled: Shephali Frost, Poetry & Song
blurb: Poetry and South Asian song on memory and migration, set loose among Mark Hewins' electric guitar, Adrian Northover's soprano sax and Ansuman Biswas on percussion.

title: Barry Lyndon on 35mm
blurb: Kubrick's candlelit costume drama on 35mm, two dates only. Three hours of exquisite misfortune.

title: Sam Gendel & Sam Wilkes
blurb: Gendel's processed, sighing sax and Wilkes' elastic bass drifting through half-remembered standards. Should sound otherworldly under the chapel's dome.

title: The Film London Jarman Award 2026
blurb: Sadia Pineda Hameed, Ilona Sagar, Rhea Storr and Alia Syed in the Assembly Room, winner named 24 November. The annual temperature check on British artists' moving image.

title: Upset The Rhythm presents: Grouper, Two-Day Residency
blurb: Liz Harris's fogbound guitar-and-voice hymns, with short films by Takashi Makino and Tanja Engelberts on night one and Coby Sey opening night two. Sold out, so it's the DICE waiting list or nothing.

title: Art Futures: Platforms for Dissent with Tania Bruguera and Pankaj Mishra
blurb: The artist who keeps getting detained in Havana and the essayist of Age of Anger on politics and dissent. A £5 livestream exists for the shy.

title: The Haunted Landscape: Magic, Fairies and Old Gods
blurb: London Fortean Society all-dayer with Ronald Hutton on the Horned God, Francis Young on fairies, Marion Gibson on witch hunts and Simon Costin of the Museum of Witchcraft. Bring a packed lunch and an open mind.

title: Abbas Zahedi, SONIC SUPPORT: ECO Performance
blurb: Abbas Zahedi's Extracorporeal Orchestra improvises on grief and care in a hospice's Mulberry Room, for staff, patients and visitors alike. Free, booking essential, and not one for chatter.

title: Andrius Arutiunian: They Tried to Count Us
blurb: A reconstructed chunk of an Armenian radio telescope's anechoic chamber and a new sound piece tuned to the stars. Free, and the quietest room on the South Bank.

title: LOST FUTURES: Wax, Or the Discovery of Television Among the Bees
blurb: David Blair's 1991 cyberpunk bee mythology, the first film ever streamed online, shown from VHS for its 35th birthday. Bootlegs on sale.

title: Nan Goldin: You Never Did Anything Wrong
blurb: Four films including two recent ones that swap the party for animals and land, her first UK institutional show since 2002. The big one worth paying for this winter.

title: Rebecca Tamás & Malcolm Gaskill: The Book of Mysteries
blurb: The poet of WITCH and the historian of England's witch trials compare notes on the unexplained. Bloomsbury's most respectable seance.

title: Unsound London: Lorenzo Senni, RP Boo & Gary Gwadera, Aleksandra Słyż
blurb: Kraków's Unsound opens its ICA residency with Senni's pointillist trance, RP Boo splicing Chicago footwork with Polish oberek (dancers from both traditions included) and Słyż premiering Ruins.

title: Wellcome Collection Lates: Not Done Yet
blurb: A late night of performance, film, talks and workshops on care and activism in the ongoing HIV response, made with Positive East. Free but ticketed, first come first served.

title: London International Animation Festival 2026
blurb: LIAF's annual sweep of the strange end of animation, from abstract shorts to adults only programmes.

title: Oneman + Plastician
blurb: Two of the selectors who joined the dots between grime, dubstep and garage on pirate radio, together in a room built for exactly that pressure.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol Sing-Along
blurb: The PCC's December institution: dozens of sing-along screenings of the definitive Dickens adaptation, right up to Christmas Eve.

title: Sonic Cinema: Daichi Saito
blurb: Three hand processed abstract landscape films projected from the artist's own 35mm prints, with Saito in conversation after.

title: Studio Ghibli All-Nighter
blurb: Totoro, Kiki, Howl, Mononoke and Spirited Away, subtitled, 565 minutes until breakfast. Bring a catbus pillow.

title: The Films of Matt Johnson Marathon
blurb: The Dirties to Blackberry to Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie, back to back overnight. A rare chance to binge Canada's most committed prankster auteur.

title: Jennifer Walshe / Tomomi Adachi + Jackson Burton
blurb: Two of the most unhinged extended vocalists alive in duo: Walshe's glossolalia and character-shifting against Adachi's sound poetry and homemade sensor instruments.

title: Jean-Francois Stevenin: Jurassic Man
blurb: The French character actor's own small, wild run of directing work, rarely screened in the UK.

title: The Lord of the Rings Trilogy [Theatrical Editions] on 35mm
blurb: All three theatrical cuts on 35mm through the night, 558 minutes to Mount Doom. Two Saturdays to choose from.

title: Makers Market
blurb: The ICA's first makers market fills the Theatre with London artists selling prints, ceramics and zines, with mulled wine for morale. The nearest thing to a December print fair we could find.

title: Gothique: Dracula (1973) + They Have Changed Their Face, intro by Kim Newman
blurb: Two deep cut Draculas: a stagey Canadian TV version and an Italian capitalist vampire allegory with Adolfo Celi. Kim Newman explains.

title: Christmas Pyjama Party
blurb: Muppet Christmas Carol, Elf, Home Alone, Gremlins and Die Hard overnight, nightwear strongly encouraged. 16+.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey in 70mm
blurb: The annual post Christmas pilgrimage: Kubrick's monolith in 70mm across the dead days between Christmas and the first weekend of January.
